questions.question: Which sentence would be *least* appropriate to include in the body of a formal complaint letter about a broken street light?

options.text: "I would like to draw your kind attention to the non-functional street light..."
options.explanation: This is a polite and appropriate way to start a complaint.

options.text: "This street light has been broken for two weeks, making the area unsafe at night."
options.explanation: This provides factual information and is appropriate for a complaint.

options.text: "Please fix this light quickly, or else we will all be very angry!"
options.explanation: This sentence uses an overly emotional and demanding tone, which is inappropriate for a formal letter.

options.text: "We kindly request your prompt action to resolve this issue."
options.explanation: This is a polite and appropriate way to end a complaint.

questions.explanation: This sentence uses an overly emotional and demanding tone ('very angry!') which is inappropriate for a formal complaint letter. Formal letters require polite and respectful language, even when complaining.
questions.hint: Formal letters should maintain a polite and respectful tone.
